name: Justice Defenders
mission: JUSTICE DEFENDERS PROVIDES LEGAL EDUCATION, TRAINING, AND PRACTICE WITHIN DEFENSELESS COMMUNITIES. FOUNDED IN 2007, JUSTICE DEFENDERS WORK ACROSS 35+ PRISONS IN AFRICA WHERE INCARCERATED PEOPLE AND OFFICERS TRAIN AND PROVIDE LEGAL SERVICES FOR THEMSELVES AND OTHERS.
theoryOfChange: Justice Defenders has a published theory of change as part of their 'The Justice Defenders Way' document on their official website. This document outlines their 2025-2027 strategy, which includes expanding their work to '10 new prisons. Including planting a prison community in the United States.' The document explicitly states 'OUR THEORY OF CHANGE' under 'Our founding documents'. The 'The Justice Defenders Way' page describes their approach to bringing justice to those in need through legal education, training, and practice within prison communities, aiming to transform prisons into places of learning and service.

strengths_deep_dive: Justice Defenders delivers cost-effective legal interventions within African prison systems <cite id="3">[3]</cite>. By training incarcerated individuals and staff as paralegals, the organization multiplies its reach, resulting in <cite id="3">12,870 releases</cite> and <cite id="4">15,338 court-ordered releases</cite> across recent reporting cycles <cite id="3">[3]</cite><cite id="4">[4]</cite>. This model yields an estimated cost per beneficiary of $9.99.
rich_narrative.summary: Justice Defenders provides legal education and training to help incarcerated individuals represent themselves in court across Africa <cite id="3">[3]</cite>. Founded in 2007, the organization operates prison legal offices and paralegal programs in countries like Kenya and Uganda <cite id="3">[3]</cite>. In FY2024, the organization reported $1,331,729 in total revenue <cite id="2">[2]</cite>. While the organization achieves tangible legal outcomes, its financial metrics reflect recent headwinds. Total revenue declined by 29% from FY2023 to FY2024 <cite id="2">[2]</cite>, while its program expense ratio stood at 58.5% in FY2024 <cite id="1">[1]</cite>. Additionally, total expenses significantly exceeded revenue in FY2023 <cite id="2">[2]</cite>. Balancing these financial challenges, Justice Defenders demonstrates high direct impact per dollar, spending approximately $9.99 per beneficiary while facilitating thousands of releases through court decisions and mediation <cite id="3">[3]</cite><cite id="4">[4]</cite>.
